chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Harun ibn Imran al-Hamadhani, who said:

There were five hundred dinars due from me to al-Nahiyah, and I became distressed because of it. Then I said to myself: I have shops which I bought for five hundred and thirty dinars; I have made them for al-Nahiyah for five hundred dinars, though I did not utter this.
So he wrote to Muhammad ibn Ja'far: Take possession of the shops from Muhammad ibn Harun for the five hundred dinars that are owed to us by him.

key_terms.النَّاحِيَةِ: a designation for the sacred authority to whom the debt was owed
key_terms.الَّتِي لَنَا عَلَيْهِ: which is owed by him to us
key_terms.حَوَانِيتُ: shops or commercial properties owned by the narrator

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the Imam’s knowledge of an unspoken intention regarding a financial debt?
ai.summary: This report narrates that Muhammad ibn Harun inwardly resolved to transfer his shops in settlement of a debt owed to al-Nahiyah. A written instruction then came confirming that very arrangement, indicating knowledge of his unspoken intention and the acceptance of the property against the amount owed.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Haroun Bin Imran Al Hamdany who said,

‘There was (a debt) upon me of five hundred Dinars for the hand (of the 12<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), and I was constricted due to it and fed up. Then I said within myself, ‘The shops which I have acquired with five hundred and thirty Dinars, I have made these to be for the hand (of the 12<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) for five hundred Dinars’, and I did not speak with it.
So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote to Muhammad Bin Ja’far: ‘Seize the shops from Muhammad Bin Haroun due to the five hundred Dinars which are for us<sup>asws</sup> upon him’.
en.sarwar: 28. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Harun ibn ‘Imran al-Hamadani who has said the following.

“I owed five hundred Dinars to the holy location (office of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.). I felt extremely depressed about it. I said to myself, “The stores that have bought was for five hundred thirty Dinars. I will set them aside for the holy location (office of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.).” However I had not said anything in words.
He wrote to Muhammad ibn Ja‘far, “Take possession of the stores from Muhammad ibn Harun as payment for the five hundred Dinars that he owed us.”
